newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil says Statfjord output normal again.
newsitem.headline: Statoil says Statfjord output normal again.

text.p: Norwegian oil company Statoil, Den norske stats oljeselskap AS, said on Sunday offshore oil loadings had been resumed at the Statfjord complex and that production was coming back to normal following stormy weather.
The high seas forced loadings to be halted on Thursday and Statoil reduced production on Friday because the storage tanks were almost full.
"The ships started loading again last night at Statfjord," Statoil spokesman Kai Nielsen said. "Production was reduced for two days but is now coming back to normal levels."

The North Sea platform pumps about 380,000 barrel per day (bpd) and processes crude from the Statfjord East and North satellites and the nearby Snorre and Vigdis developments, which in total add roughly 400,000 bpd to the Statfjord stream.
